items.title: Stop Driving Immediately
items.description: In some situations, engine vibration can indicate a serious problem. Stop driving immediately if you notice any of the following symptoms.

blocks.text: Do Not Continue Driving If You Experience:

🚨 Critical warning - internal imbalance: If the whole car shakes violently and the vibration increases with engine RPM, stop driving immediately. This indicates a broken crankshaft, connecting rod failure, or a dropped valve. Continued driving will cause complete engine destruction (£2,500-£6,500+).

🚨 Flashing EML + vibration: If your engine management light is flashing while the engine vibrates, unburnt fuel is destroying your catalytic converter (petrol) or DPF (diesel). Stop driving immediately - repair cost escalates from £60-£800 to £1,000-£2,500.

items.title: Vibration at Idle
items.description: Engine mounts are rubber and hydraulic components that isolate engine vibration from the chassis. When they wear, crack, or collapse, the engine transmits vibration directly to the body - felt most strongly at idle.

blocks.text: Vibration pattern: Steering wheel or seat vibration when stationary. Vibration reduces or disappears when driving. May also hear a clunk when accelerating or decelerating as the engine rocks on broken mounts.

rows: Premium / Large SUV (Range Rover, X5, Q7)

blocks.text: Specialist rule of thumb: "If you feel vibration at idle but the engine runs smoothly when revved in neutral, it's almost always engine mounts. A £200-£500 fix. Don't let anyone sell you spark plugs or injectors for idle vibration."
Get a quote from our network of trusted UK specialists.

items.title: Vibration Under Acceleration
items.description: One or more cylinders aren't firing correctly. The engine runs unevenly, producing a shaking or jerking sensation - most noticeable under load (acceleration, uphill).

blocks.text: Vibration pattern: Engine shakes under acceleration, especially between 1,500-3,000 RPM. May be smooth at idle. Often accompanied by loss of power, poor fuel economy, and potentially a flashing engine management light.

rows: Ford EcoBoost, VW TSI, BMW N-series

blocks.text: • Vibration under acceleration, smooth at idle

Specialist rule of thumb (petrol): "On a petrol engine with vibration under acceleration, swap the ignition coil with another cylinder. If the vibration moves, it's a £70-£220 coil. If it doesn't move, check spark plugs first - a full set is £50-£150."
Severe vibration can lead to expensive damage. Get expert advice before it's too late.

items.title: Vibration on Clutch Engagement
items.description: The dual-mass flywheel absorbs torsional vibration from the engine. When its internal springs or bearings fail, it produces vibration specifically when engaging the clutch or during gear changes.

blocks.text: Vibration pattern: Vibration or judder when pulling away from a stop. Rattle or knocking noise at idle that disappears when the clutch pedal is pressed.

Specialist rule of thumb: "If you hear a rattle at idle that goes away when you press the clutch, it's almost always the dual-mass flywheel. Replace the clutch at the same time - the gearbox is already off, and you'll pay the same labour."

items.title: Finding the Cause
items.description: A systematic approach helps identify the real cause of engine vibration.

blocks.text: Scan with an OBD2 reader for pending or active trouble codes.
Inspect hoses, mounts, wiring and visible mechanical components.
Check for collapsed rubber, excessive movement or hydraulic leakage.
Examine spark plugs, coil packs, and injector spray balances.
Check DMF play, drive shafts, universal joints, and gearbox bushes.

Diagnostic rule: "Never replace engine mounts based on vibration alone. A misfire can feel like a shaky engine mount at idle. Always do an OBD2 scan first - it's £50-£120 and will tell you if there's a misfire code before you spend £150-£500 on mounts that won't fix the problem."
